html:
Thomas Mofolo was a Mosotho writer whose novel Chaka, about the Zulu king Shaka, is one of the first major novels written in an African language.

Educated at the mission school of Morija, he worked as a teacher and proofreader at the mission press, which published his first novels in Sesotho. He wrote Chaka in about 1910, but the missionaries delayed it for years, uneasy at its picture of Shaka's power and ambition, and it came out only in 1925.

The novel portrays Shaka as a tragic figure ruined by ambition. It was translated into English, French and other languages and shaped how later African writers told the story of the Zulu king. It stands at the start of written literature in Sesotho and in Lesotho.
sum: Thomas Mofolo was a Mosotho writer whose novel Chaka, about the Zulu king Shaka, is one of the first major novels written in an African language.
